# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.

**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function accepts a single string parameter
- Function returns a string
- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
- Function handles empty strings gracefully
- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)

### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"

### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores

### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
- Numbers (0-9) are retained
- Hyphens (-) are retained
- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)

### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"

### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"

### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Empty input string "" returns ""
- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
- No exceptions or errors are thrown

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title

**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
- THEN I receive "hello-world"

### STORY-002: Normalize File Names

**As a** developer processing user uploads
**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators

**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN input "a---b"
- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
- THEN I receive "a-b"

### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases

**As a** developer
**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions

## Business Rules

### BR-001: Transformation Order
The transformations must be applied in the following order:
1. Convert to lowercase
2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens

### BR-002: Character Whitelist
Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
- Lowercase letters: a-z
- Numbers: 0-9
- Hyphen: -

### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
The function must never throw exceptions for any string input. Invalid or problematic input should result in an empty string or a valid slug.

## Examples & Test Cases

| Input | Expected Output | Test Focus |
|-------|----------------|------------|
| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | Basic punctuation removal |
| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" | Underscore replacement |
| "a---b" | "a-b" | Hyphen collapsing |

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe slug strings through a deterministic transformation pipeline (lowercase -> replace separators -> filter characters -> collapse hyphens -> trim). The function follows existing codebase patterns with no external dependencies and comprehensive test coverage.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> Lower["1. toLowerCase()"]
    Lower --> Replace["2. Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]
    Replace --> Filter["3. Remove non-alphanumeric (except hyphens)"]
    Filter --> Collapse["4. Collapse consecutive hyphens"]
    Collapse --> Trim["5. Trim leading/trailing hyphens"]
    Trim --> Output["Output Slug"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | src/utils.ts | Any module | `(text: string) => string` - pure, synchronous, never throws |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing 5-step transformation pipeline per BR-001 | src/utils.ts |
| T2 | Unit tests | Comprehensive test coverage for all requirements and edge cases | src/utils.test.ts |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Core function implementation

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface: tests import slugify function from utils.ts)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Case normalization (REQ-002) | Mixed case not lowercased | unit | `bun test` - "Hello" -> "hello" |
| Whitespace replacement (REQ-003) | Spaces/underscores not replaced | unit | `bun test` - "Foo Bar", "Foo__Bar" |
| Character filtering (REQ-004) | Special chars remain in output | unit | `bun test` - "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |
| Hyphen collapsing (REQ-005) | Multiple hyphens not collapsed | unit | `bun test` - "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Hyphen trimming (REQ-006) | Leading/trailing hyphens remain | unit | `bun test` - "-hello-" -> "hello" |
| Empty input handling (REQ-007) | Throws on empty/invalid input | unit | `bun test` - "", "!!!", "   " all return "" |
| Transformation order (BR-001) | Wrong order produces wrong output | unit | `bun test` - combined cases verify order |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | .rp1/context/modules.md | Utils | modules.md:Utils | Add slugify to utils module description |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Unicode input produces unexpected results | LOW | Explicitly out of scope per requirements; non-ASCII filtered out |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation approach | Chained string methods | Simple, readable, follows existing utils.ts style; performance not a concern per requirements | Single regex with multiple capture groups (more complex, harder to maintain) |
| D2 | Regex vs iterative | Regex replacements | More concise and idiomatic TypeScript; matches transformation rules directly | Character-by-character iteration (more verbose, no benefit) |
| D3 | Test organization | Single describe block with test per requirement | Matches existing test style in utils.test.ts; clear traceability to requirements | Separate describe blocks per transformation (overkill for single function) |
| D4 | Edge case handling | Return empty string | Explicit requirement (REQ-007); consistent with transformation pipeline | Throw error (violates BR-003), return placeholder like "untitled" (not specified) |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| File location | src/utils.ts | KB modules.md | Utils module is the documented location for reusable utility functions |
| Test location | src/utils.test.ts | KB patterns.md | Tests co-located with source as *.test.ts per project patterns |
| Test framework | Bun built-in test | KB patterns.md | Project uses Bun's built-in test runner with describe/test/expect |
| Function naming | camelCase (slugify) | KB patterns.md | Functions use camelCase per naming conventions |
| No external deps | Built-in String methods only | KB patterns.md, requirements | Project explicitly avoids external dependencies |

     7→---
     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"
    99→
   100→### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   101→
   102→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   103→**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
   104→**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
   105→**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
   106→
   107→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   108→- Empty input string "" returns ""
   109→- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   120→
   121→**Acceptance**:
   122→- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
   123→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads
   129→**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:
   133→- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:
   155→- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
   156→- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
   157→- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions
   158→
   159→## Business Rules
   160→
   161→### BR-001: Transformation Order
   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z
   172→- Numbers: 0-9
   173→- Hyphen: -
   174→
   175→### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
   176→The function must never throw exceptions for any string input. Invalid or problematic input should result in an empty string or a valid slug.
   177→
   178→## Examples & Test Cases
   179→
   180→| Input | Expected Output | Test Focus |
   181→|-------|----------------|------------|
   182→| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | Basic punctuation removal |
   183→| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" | Underscore replacement |
   184→| "a---b" | "a-b" | Hyphen collapsing |
   185→| "  Leading Space" | "leading-space" | Leading space handling |
   186→| "Trailing Space  " | "trailing-space" | Trailing space handling |
   187→| "MixedCase123" | "mixedcase123" | Case normalization with numbers |
   188→| "!!!" | "" | All special characters |
   189→| "" | "" | Empty string |
   190→| "one two  three" | "one-two-three" | Multiple spaces |
   191→| "-hyphen-" | "hyphen" | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |
   192→| "café" | "caf" | Non-ASCII characters (if applicable) |
   193→
   194→## Constraints & Assumptions
   195→
   196→**Constraints**:
   197→- Function must be synchronous
   198→- Function must be stateless and pure
   199→- No external dependencies (use only language built-ins)
   200→- Must work with TypeScript/Bun environment
   201→
   202→**Assumptions**:
   203→- Input is always a string (no type validation required)
   204→- ASCII characters only (no Unicode normalization for accented characters)
   205→- Performance is not critical (simple implementation acceptable)
   206→- Function will be exported from the utility module
   207→
   208→## Out of Scope
   209→
   210→The following are explicitly NOT part of this requirement:
   211→- Unicode/international character support (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   212→- Custom separator characters (always uses hyphen)
   213→- Maximum length limiting or truncation
   214→- Collision detection or uniqueness guarantees
   215→- Database integration
   216→- URL encoding beyond basic slug transformation
   217→
   218→## Success Metrics
   219→
   220→**Definition of Done**:
   221→- [ ] Function is implemented in `src/utils.ts`
   222→- [ ] All example test cases pass
   223→- [ ] Function signature matches: `slugify(text: string): string`
   224→- [ ] Unit tests cover all requirements and edge cases
   225→- [ ] Function is exported and available for use
   226→
   227→**Quality Criteria**:
   228→- Test coverage for all transformation rules
   229→- Edge cases handled without errors
   230→- Code is simple and maintainable
   231→- Examples from requirements all produce correct output
   232→
   233→## AFK Mode Decisions
   234→
   235→This requirements document was generated in AFK (autonomous) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:
   236→
   237→### Decision 1: No PRD Association
   238→**Context**: No PRD directory was found at `.rp1/work/prds/`
   239→**Decision**: Proceeded without parent PRD association
   240→**Rationale**: The feature request is self-contained with clear specifications. The provided examples and transformation rules are sufficient to define complete requirements.
   241→
   242→### Decision 2: Character Set Scope
   243→**Context**: Input specification mentions "letters" and "numbers" without defining Unicode handling
   244→**Decision**: Assumed ASCII-only character set (a-z, 0-9)
   245→**Rationale**: The project is TypeScript-based and examples only show ASCII characters. Unicode normalization (e.g., é→e) adds complexity and wasn't explicitly required.
   246→
   247→### Decision 3: Input Validation
   248→**Context**: No mention of how to handle non-string inputs
   249→**Decision**: Assumed input is always a valid string; no type checking required
   250→**Rationale**: TypeScript provides compile-time type safety. Runtime type validation would be redundant in a typed environment.
   251→
   252→### Decision 4: Empty Result Handling
   253→**Context**: Not specified what to return when all characters are filtered out
   254→**Decision**: Return empty string ""
   255→**Rationale**: Most consistent with the transformation pipeline. Allows calling code to check for empty slugs and handle as needed.
   256→
   257→### Decision 5: Transformation Order
   258→**Context**: Transformation rules were listed but order not explicitly specified
   259→**Decision**: Applied in the order: lowercase → replace → filter → collapse → trim
   260→**Rationale**: This order ensures correct behavior (e.g., spaces must be replaced before collapsing hyphens, collapsing must happen before trimming).

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"
    99→
   100→### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   101→
   102→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   103→**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
   104→**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
   105→**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
   106→
   107→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   108→- Empty input string "" returns ""
   109→- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   120→

   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads

   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:

   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:
   155→- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)

   157→- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions
   158→
   159→## Business Rules
   160→
   161→### BR-001: Transformation Order
   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z

   173→- Hyphen: -
   174→
   175→### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"
    99→
   100→### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   101→
   102→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   103→**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
   104→**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
   105→**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
   106→
   107→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   108→- Empty input string "" returns ""
   109→- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   120→
   121→**Acceptance**:
   122→- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
   123→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads
   129→**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:
   133→- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:
   155→- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
   156→- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
   157→- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions
   158→
   159→## Business Rules
   160→
   161→### BR-001: Transformation Order
   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z
   172→- Numbers: 0-9
   173→- Hyphen: -
   174→
   175→### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
   176→The function must never throw exceptions for any string input. Invalid or problematic input should result in an empty string or a valid slug.
   177→
   178→## Examples & Test Cases
   179→
   180→| Input | Expected Output | Test Focus |
   181→|-------|----------------|------------|
   182→| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | Basic punctuation removal |
   183→| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" | Underscore replacement |
   184→| "a---b" | "a-b" | Hyphen collapsing |
   185→| "  Leading Space" | "leading-space" | Leading space handling |
   186→| "Trailing Space  " | "trailing-space" | Trailing space handling |
   187→| "MixedCase123" | "mixedcase123" | Case normalization with numbers |
   188→| "!!!" | "" | All special characters |
   189→| "" | "" | Empty string |
   190→| "one two  three" | "one-two-three" | Multiple spaces |
   191→| "-hyphen-" | "hyphen" | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |
   192→| "café" | "caf" | Non-ASCII characters (if applicable) |
   193→
   194→## Constraints & Assumptions
   195→
   196→**Constraints**:
   197→- Function must be synchronous
   198→- Function must be stateless and pure
   199→- No external dependencies (use only language built-ins)
   200→- Must work with TypeScript/Bun environment
   201→
   202→**Assumptions**:
   203→- Input is always a string (no type validation required)
   204→- ASCII characters only (no Unicode normalization for accented characters)
   205→- Performance is not critical (simple implementation acceptable)
   206→- Function will be exported from the utility module
   207→
   208→## Out of Scope
   209→
   210→The following are explicitly NOT part of this requirement:
   211→- Unicode/international character support (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   212→- Custom separator characters (always uses hyphen)
   213→- Maximum length limiting or truncation
   214→- Collision detection or uniqueness guarantees
   215→- Database integration
   216→- URL encoding beyond basic slug transformation
   217→
   218→## Success Metrics

   220→**Definition of Done**:
   221→- [ ] Function is implemented in `src/utils.ts`
   222→- [ ] All example test cases pass
   223→- [ ] Function signature matches: `slugify(text: string): string`
   224→- [ ] Unit tests cover all requirements and edge cases
   225→- [ ] Function is exported and available for use
   226→
   227→**Quality Criteria**:
   228→- Test coverage for all transformation rules
   229→- Edge cases handled without errors
   230→- Code is simple and maintainable
   231→- Examples from requirements all produce correct output
   232→
   233→## AFK Mode Decisions

   235→This requirements document was generated in AFK (autonomous) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"
    99→
   100→### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   101→
   102→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   103→**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
   104→**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
   105→**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
   106→
   107→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   108→- Empty input string "" returns ""
   109→- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   120→
   121→**Acceptance**:
   122→- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
   123→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads
   129→**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:
   133→- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:
   155→- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
   156→- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
   157→- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions
   158→
   159→## Business Rules
   160→
   161→### BR-001: Transformation Order
   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z
   172→- Numbers: 0-9
   173→- Hyphen: -
   174→
   175→### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
   176→The function must never throw exceptions for any string input. Invalid or problematic input should result in an empty string or a valid slug.
   177→
   178→## Examples & Test Cases
   179→
   180→| Input | Expected Output | Test Focus |
   181→|-------|----------------|------------|
   182→| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | Basic punctuation removal |
   183→| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" | Underscore replacement |
   184→| "a---b" | "a-b" | Hyphen collapsing |
   185→| "  Leading Space" | "leading-space" | Leading space handling |
   186→| "Trailing Space  " | "trailing-space" | Trailing space handling |
   187→| "MixedCase123" | "mixedcase123" | Case normalization with numbers |
   188→| "!!!" | "" | All special characters |
   189→| "" | "" | Empty string |
   190→| "one two  three" | "one-two-three" | Multiple spaces |
   191→| "-hyphen-" | "hyphen" | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |
   192→| "café" | "caf" | Non-ASCII characters (if applicable) |
   193→
   194→## Constraints & Assumptions
   195→
   196→**Constraints**:
   197→- Function must be synchronous
   198→- Function must be stateless and pure
   199→- No external dependencies (use only language built-ins)
   200→- Must work with TypeScript/Bun environment
   201→
   202→**Assumptions**:
   203→- Input is always a string (no type validation required)
   204→- ASCII characters only (no Unicode normalization for accented characters)
   205→- Performance is not critical (simple implementation acceptable)
   206→- Function will be exported from the utility module
   207→
   208→## Out of Scope
   209→
   210→The following are explicitly NOT part of this requirement:
   211→- Unicode/international character support (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   212→- Custom separator characters (always uses hyphen)
   213→- Maximum length limiting or truncation
   214→- Collision detection or uniqueness guarantees
   215→- Database integration
   216→- URL encoding beyond basic slug transformation
   217→
   218→## Success Metrics
   219→
   220→**Definition of Done**:
   221→- [ ] Function is implemented in `src/utils.ts`
   222→- [ ] All example test cases pass
   223→- [ ] Function signature matches: `slugify(text: string): string`
   224→- [ ] Unit tests cover all requirements and edge cases
   225→- [ ] Function is exported and available for use
   226→
   227→**Quality Criteria**:
   228→- Test coverage for all transformation rules
   229→- Edge cases handled without errors
   230→- Code is simple and maintainable
   231→- Examples from requirements all produce correct output
   232→
   233→## AFK Mode Decisions
   234→
   235→This requirements document was generated in AFK (autonomous) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:
   236→
   237→### Decision 1: No PRD Association
   238→**Context**: No PRD directory was found at `.rp1/work/prds/`
   239→**Decision**: Proceeded without parent PRD association
   240→**Rationale**: The feature request is self-contained with clear specifications. The provided examples and transformation rules are sufficient to define complete requirements.
   241→
   242→### Decision 2: Character Set Scope
   243→**Context**: Input specification mentions "letters" and "numbers" without defining Unicode handling
   244→**Decision**: Assumed ASCII-only character set (a-z, 0-9)
   245→**Rationale**: The project is TypeScript-based and examples only show ASCII characters. Unicode normalization (e.g., é→e) adds complexity and wasn't explicitly required.
   246→
   247→### Decision 3: Input Validation
   248→**Context**: No mention of how to handle non-string inputs
   249→**Decision**: Assumed input is always a valid string; no type checking required
   250→**Rationale**: TypeScript provides compile-time type safety. Runtime type validation would be redundant in a typed environment.
   251→
   252→### Decision 4: Empty Result Handling
   253→**Context**: Not specified what to return when all characters are filtered out
   254→**Decision**: Return empty string ""
   255→**Rationale**: Most consistent with the transformation pipeline. Allows calling code to check for empty slugs and handle as needed.
   256→
   257→### Decision 5: Transformation Order
   258→**Context**: Transformation rules were listed but order not explicitly specified
   259→**Decision**: Applied in the order: lowercase → replace → filter → collapse → trim
   260→**Rationale**: This order ensures correct behavior (e.g., spaces must be replaced before collapsing hyphens, collapsing must happen before trimming).
   261→
   262→## Notes
   263→
   264→- This is a utility function suitable for the existing `src/utils.ts` module based on the project structure documented in the knowledge base
   265→- The function should be accompanied by comprehensive tests in `src/utils.test.ts` following the project's testing patterns

# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.

**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function accepts a single string parameter
- Function returns a string
- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
- Function handles empty strings gracefully
- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)

### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"

### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores

### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
- Numbers (0-9) are retained
- Hyphens (-) are retained
- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)

### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"

### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"

### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]

**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Empty input string "" returns ""
- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
- No exceptions or errors are thrown

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title

**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
- THEN I receive "hello-world"

### STORY-002: Normalize File Names

**As a** developer processing user uploads
**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators

**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN input "a---b"
- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
- THEN I receive "a-b"

### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases

**As a** developer
**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input

**Acceptance**:
- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions

## Business Rules

### BR-001: Transformation Order
The transformations must be applied in the following order:
1. Convert to lowercase
2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens

### BR-002: Character Whitelist
Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
- Lowercase letters: a-z
- Numbers: 0-9
- Hyphen: -

### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
The function must never throw exceptions for any string input. Invalid or problematic input should result in an empty string or a valid slug.

## Examples & Test Cases

| Input | Expected Output | Test Focus |
|-------|----------------|------------|
| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | Basic punctuation removal |
| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" | Underscore replacement |
| "a---b" | "a-b" | Hyphen collapsing |
| "  Leading Space" | "leading-space" | Leading space handling |
| "Trailing Space  " | "trailing-space" | Trailing space handling |
| "MixedCase123" | "mixedcase123" | Case normalization with numbers |
| "!!!" | "" | All special characters |
| "" | "" | Empty string |
| "one two  three" | "one-two-three" | Multiple spaces |
| "-hyphen-" | "hyphen" | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |
| "café" | "caf" | Non-ASCII characters (if applicable) |

## Constraints & Assumptions

**Constraints**:
- Function must be synchronous
- Function must be stateless and pure
- No external dependencies (use only language built-ins)
- Must work with TypeScript/Bun environment

**Assumptions**:
- Input is always a string (no type validation required)
- ASCII characters only (no Unicode normalization for accented characters)
- Performance is not critical (simple implementation acceptable)
- Function will be exported from the utility module

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly NOT part of this requirement:
- Unicode/international character support (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
- Custom separator characters (always uses hyphen)
- Maximum length limiting or truncation
- Collision detection or uniqueness guarantees
- Database integration
- URL encoding beyond basic slug transformation

## Success Metrics

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] Function is implemented in `src/utils.ts`
- [ ] All example test cases pass
- [ ] Function signature matches: `slugify(text: string): string`
- [ ] Unit tests cover all requirements and edge cases
- [ ] Function is exported and available for use

**Quality Criteria**:
- Test coverage for all transformation rules
- Edge cases handled without errors
- Code is simple and maintainable
- Examples from requirements all produce correct output

## AFK Mode Decisions

This requirements document was generated in AFK (autonomous) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:

### Decision 1: No PRD Association
**Context**: No PRD directory was found at `.rp1/work/prds/`
**Decision**: Proceeded without parent PRD association
**Rationale**: The feature request is self-contained with clear specifications. The provided examples and transformation rules are sufficient to define complete requirements.

### Decision 2: Character Set Scope
**Context**: Input specification mentions "letters" and "numbers" without defining Unicode handling
**Decision**: Assumed ASCII-only character set (a-z, 0-9)
**Rationale**: The project is TypeScript-based and examples only show ASCII characters. Unicode normalization (e.g., é→e) adds complexity and wasn't explicitly required.

### Decision 3: Input Validation
**Context**: No mention of how to handle non-string inputs
**Decision**: Assumed input is always a valid string; no type checking required
**Rationale**: TypeScript provides compile-time type safety. Runtime type validation would be redundant in a typed environment.

### Decision 4: Empty Result Handling
**Context**: Not specified what to return when all characters are filtered out
**Decision**: Return empty string ""
**Rationale**: Most consistent with the transformation pipeline. Allows calling code to check for empty slugs and handle as needed.

### Decision 5: Transformation Order
**Context**: Transformation rules were listed but order not explicitly specified
**Decision**: Applied in the order: lowercase → replace → filter → collapse → trim
**Rationale**: This order ensures correct behavior (e.g., spaces must be replaced before collapsing hyphens, collapsing must happen before trimming).

## Notes

- This is a utility function suitable for the existing `src/utils.ts` module based on the project structure documented in the knowledge base
- The function should be accompanied by comprehensive tests in `src/utils.test.ts` following the project's testing patterns
- The simple, pure function design aligns with the "Utility scripting" domain concept

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe slug strings through a deterministic transformation pipeline (lowercase -> replace separators -> filter characters -> collapse hyphens -> trim). The function follows existing codebase patterns with no external dependencies and comprehensive test coverage.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> Lower["1. toLowerCase()"]
    Lower --> Replace["2. Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]
    Replace --> Filter["3. Remove non-alphanumeric (except hyphens)"]
    Filter --> Collapse["4. Collapse consecutive hyphens"]
    Collapse --> Trim["5. Trim leading/trailing hyphens"]
    Trim --> Output["Output Slug"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | src/utils.ts | Any module | `(text: string) => string` - pure, synchronous, never throws |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing 5-step transformation pipeline per BR-001 | src/utils.ts |
| T2 | Unit tests | Comprehensive test coverage for all requirements and edge cases | src/utils.test.ts |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Core function implementation

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface: tests import slugify function from utils.ts)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Case normalization (REQ-002) | Mixed case not lowercased | unit | `bun test` - "Hello" -> "hello" |
| Whitespace replacement (REQ-003) | Spaces/underscores not replaced | unit | `bun test` - "Foo Bar", "Foo__Bar" |
| Character filtering (REQ-004) | Special chars remain in output | unit | `bun test` - "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |
| Hyphen collapsing (REQ-005) | Multiple hyphens not collapsed | unit | `bun test` - "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Hyphen trimming (REQ-006) | Leading/trailing hyphens remain | unit | `bun test` - "-hello-" -> "hello" |
| Empty input handling (REQ-007) | Throws on empty/invalid input | unit | `bun test` - "", "!!!", "   " all return "" |
| Transformation order (BR-001) | Wrong order produces wrong output | unit | `bun test` - combined cases verify order |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | .rp1/context/modules.md | Utils | modules.md:Utils | Add slugify to utils module description |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Unicode input produces unexpected results | LOW | Explicitly out of scope per requirements; non-ASCII filtered out |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation approach | Chained string methods | Simple, readable, follows existing utils.ts style; performance not a concern per requirements | Single regex with multiple capture groups (more complex, harder to maintain) |

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"

   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages

   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads
   129→**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:
   133→- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:

   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z
   172→- Numbers: 0-9
   173→- Hyphen: -
   174→
   175→### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
