     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"
    99→
   100→### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   101→
   102→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   103→**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
   104→**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
   105→**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
   106→
   107→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   108→- Empty input string "" returns ""
   109→- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   120→
   121→**Acceptance**:
   122→- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
   123→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads
   129→**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:
   133→- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:
   155→- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
   156→- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
   157→- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions
   158→
   159→## Business Rules
   160→
   161→### BR-001: Transformation Order
   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z
   172→- Numbers: 0-9
   173→- Hyphen: -

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"
    99→
   100→### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   101→
   102→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   103→**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
   104→**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
   105→**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
   106→
   107→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   108→- Empty input string "" returns ""
   109→- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   120→
   121→**Acceptance**:
   122→- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
   123→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads
   129→**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:
   133→- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:
   155→- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
   156→- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
   157→- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions
   158→
   159→## Business Rules
   160→
   161→### BR-001: Transformation Order
   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z
   172→- Numbers: 0-9
   173→- Hyphen: -
   174→
   175→### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
   176→The function must never throw exceptions for any string input. Invalid or problematic input should result in an empty string or a valid slug.
   177→
   178→## Examples & Test Cases
   179→
   180→| Input | Expected Output | Test Focus |
   181→|-------|----------------|------------|
   182→| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | Basic punctuation removal |
   183→| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" | Underscore replacement |
   184→| "a---b" | "a-b" | Hyphen collapsing |
   185→| "  Leading Space" | "leading-space" | Leading space handling |
   186→| "Trailing Space  " | "trailing-space" | Trailing space handling |
   187→| "MixedCase123" | "mixedcase123" | Case normalization with numbers |
   188→| "!!!" | "" | All special characters |
   189→| "" | "" | Empty string |
   190→| "one two  three" | "one-two-three" | Multiple spaces |
   191→| "-hyphen-" | "hyphen" | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |
   192→| "café" | "caf" | Non-ASCII characters (if applicable) |
   193→
   194→## Constraints & Assumptions
   195→
   196→**Constraints**:
   197→- Function must be synchronous
   198→- Function must be stateless and pure
   199→- No external dependencies (use only language built-ins)
   200→- Must work with TypeScript/Bun environment

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature**: String Slugification Utility
    14→**Purpose**: Provide a reusable utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, filesystem-safe, and human-readable slug strings.
    15→
    16→**Business Context**: Slugs are commonly needed for generating clean URLs, file names, identifiers, and other scenarios where readable, normalized strings are required. This utility will provide consistent slug generation across the codebase.
    17→
    18→## Functional Requirements
    19→
    20→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    21→
    22→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    23→**Action**: Call `slugify(text)` with any input string
    24→**Outcome**: Function returns a normalized slug string following all transformation rules
    25→**Rationale**: Developers need a reliable way to convert user-generated or arbitrary text into safe, consistent identifiers for URLs, file paths, and database keys.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Function accepts a single string parameter
    29→- Function returns a string
    30→- All transformation rules are applied in the correct order
    31→- Function handles empty strings gracefully
    32→- Function is pure (no side effects, same input always produces same output)
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Case Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    35→
    36→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    37→**Action**: Pass text with mixed case characters
    38→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters are converted to lowercase
    39→**Rationale**: Slugs should be case-insensitive and consistent to avoid confusion and duplication.
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- Uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    43→- Already lowercase letters remain unchanged
    44→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by this transformation
    45→- Example: "Hello World" contains lowercase "h", "e", "l", "l", "o"
    46→
    47→### REQ-003: Whitespace Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    48→
    49→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    50→**Action**: Pass text containing spaces or underscores
    51→**Outcome**: All spaces and underscores are replaced with hyphens
    52→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the conventional word separator in slugs, improving readability and SEO.
    53→
    54→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    55→- Single space character becomes a single hyphen
    56→- Multiple consecutive spaces each become a hyphen (will be collapsed later)
    57→- Underscore character (_) becomes a hyphen
    58→- Example: "Foo Bar" becomes "foo-bar", "Foo__Bar" has hyphens in place of underscores
    59→
    60→### REQ-004: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    61→
    62→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Action**: Pass text containing special characters, punctuation, or symbols
    64→**Outcome**: Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) remain in the output
    65→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, file systems, and databases. Filtering ensures maximum compatibility.
    66→
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Letters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    69→- Numbers (0-9) are retained
    70→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    71→- All other characters (!, ?, @, #, $, %, &, *, etc.) are removed
    72→- Example: "Hello, World!" becomes "hello--world" (before hyphen collapsing)
    73→
    74→### REQ-005: Hyphen Collapsing [MUST HAVE]
    75→
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**Action**: Pass text that results in consecutive hyphens after previous transformations
    78→**Outcome**: Multiple consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen
    79→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and are unnecessary for separation.
    80→
    81→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    82→- Two consecutive hyphens (--) become one hyphen (-)
    83→- Three or more consecutive hyphens become one hyphen (-)
    84→- This collapse happens after all other replacements and removals
    85→- Example: "a---b" becomes "a-b"
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    88→
    89→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    90→**Action**: Pass text that results in leading or trailing hyphens
    91→**Outcome**: Leading and trailing hyphens are removed from the final slug
    92→**Rationale**: Slugs should not start or end with separators, which looks unprofessional and can cause parsing issues.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Hyphens at the start of the string are removed
    96→- Hyphens at the end of the string are removed
    97→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
    98→- Example: "-hello-world-" becomes "hello-world"
    99→
   100→### REQ-007: Empty Input Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   101→
   102→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   103→**Action**: Pass an empty string or a string that becomes empty after processing
   104→**Outcome**: Function returns an empty string without errors
   105→**Rationale**: Edge cases must be handled gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
   106→
   107→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   108→- Empty input string "" returns ""
   109→- String with only special characters (e.g., "!!!") returns ""
   110→- String with only spaces (e.g., "   ") returns ""
   111→- No exceptions or errors are thrown
   112→
   113→## User Stories
   114→
   115→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Safe Slug from Title
   116→
   117→**As a** developer building a blog or CMS
   118→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   119→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   120→
   121→**Acceptance**:
   122→- GIVEN a title "Hello, World!"
   123→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   124→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   125→
   126→### STORY-002: Normalize File Names
   127→
   128→**As a** developer processing user uploads
   129→**I want** to convert arbitrary file names into safe slugs
   130→**So that** I can avoid file system conflicts and special character issues
   131→
   132→**Acceptance**:
   133→- GIVEN a file name "Foo__Bar.txt"
   134→- WHEN I extract the name part and call `slugify("Foo__Bar")`
   135→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   136→
   137→### STORY-003: Clean Up Multiple Separators
   138→
   139→**As a** developer receiving inconsistent input
   140→**I want** multiple consecutive separators to be normalized
   141→**So that** slugs are consistent regardless of input formatting
   142→
   143→**Acceptance**:
   144→- GIVEN input "a---b"
   145→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   146→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   147→
   148→### STORY-004: Handle Edge Cases
   149→
   150→**As a** developer
   151→**I want** the slugify function to handle edge cases gracefully
   152→**So that** my application doesn't crash on unexpected input
   153→
   154→**Acceptance**:
   155→- GIVEN various edge cases (empty strings, all special chars, etc.)
   156→- WHEN I call `slugify()` with these inputs
   157→- THEN I receive valid output without exceptions
   158→
   159→## Business Rules
   160→
   161→### BR-001: Transformation Order
   162→The transformations must be applied in the following order:
   163→1. Convert to lowercase
   164→2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   165→3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   166→4. Collapse consecutive hyphens
   167→5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   168→
   169→### BR-002: Character Whitelist
   170→Only the following characters are permitted in the final slug:
   171→- Lowercase letters: a-z
   172→- Numbers: 0-9
   173→- Hyphen: -
   174→
   175→### BR-003: No Exceptions for Invalid Input
   176→The function must never throw exceptions for any string input. Invalid or problematic input should result in an empty string or a valid slug.
   177→
   178→## Examples & Test Cases
   179→
   180→| Input | Expected Output | Test Focus |
   181→|-------|----------------|------------|
   182→| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | Basic punctuation removal |
   183→| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" | Underscore replacement |
   184→| "a---b" | "a-b" | Hyphen collapsing |
   185→| "  Leading Space" | "leading-space" | Leading space handling |
   186→| "Trailing Space  " | "trailing-space" | Trailing space handling |
   187→| "MixedCase123" | "mixedcase123" | Case normalization with numbers |
   188→| "!!!" | "" | All special characters |
   189→| "" | "" | Empty string |
   190→| "one two  three" | "one-two-three" | Multiple spaces |
   191→| "-hyphen-" | "hyphen" | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |
   192→| "café" | "caf" | Non-ASCII characters (if applicable) |
   193→
   194→## Constraints & Assumptions
   195→
   196→**Constraints**:
   197→- Function must be synchronous
   198→- Function must be stateless and pure
   199→- No external dependencies (use only language built-ins)
   200→- Must work with TypeScript/Bun environment
   201→
   202→**Assumptions**:
   203→- Input is always a string (no type validation required)
   204→- ASCII characters only (no Unicode normalization for accented characters)
   205→- Performance is not critical (simple implementation acceptable)
   206→- Function will be exported from the utility module
   207→
   208→## Out of Scope
   209→
   210→The following are explicitly NOT part of this requirement:
   211→- Unicode/international character support (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   212→- Custom separator characters (always uses hyphen)
   213→- Maximum length limiting or truncation
   214→- Collision detection or uniqueness guarantees
   215→- Database integration
   216→- URL encoding beyond basic slug transformation
   217→
   218→## Success Metrics

   220→**Definition of Done**:
   221→- [ ] Function is implemented in `src/utils.ts`
   222→- [ ] All example test cases pass
   223→- [ ] Function signature matches: `slugify(text: string): string`
   224→- [ ] Unit tests cover all requirements and edge cases
   225→- [ ] Function is exported and available for use
   226→
   227→**Quality Criteria**:
   228→- Test coverage for all transformation rules
   229→- Edge cases handled without errors
   230→- Code is simple and maintainable
   231→- Examples from requirements all produce correct output
   232→
   233→## AFK Mode Decisions
   234→
